title: Comida — pedí en un restaurante
goals: Meta declarada por el material: saber pedir comida en un restaurante.
Aprendé el vocabulario de comida y envases, distinguí contables de incontables y cuantificá con precisión.
Cerrá escribiendo y contando cómo se come en Argentina.

aspects.title: Comida y bebida
aspects.summary: Las 25 palabras del banco oficial, incluidos los pares americano/británico (cookies/biscuits, fries/chips).

aspects.title: Envases y porciones
aspects.summary: Las 24 palabras que permiten contar lo incontable: a piece of, a bar of, a carton of.

aspects.title: Contables e incontables
aspects.summary: Qué se cuenta y qué no — incluido el inglés que vas a necesitar: mathematics is, research is, much data.

aspects.title: Cuantificadores
aspects.summary: some/any, much/many, a lot of, a few/a little, no/none.

aspects.title: En el restaurante
aspects.summary: La meta de la unidad: pedir mesa, ordenar, preguntar por un plato y contar cómo se come acá.

source.note: Par mínimo nuestro: /uː/ vs /oʊ/. Trampa clásica del hispanohablante con el vocabulario de comida.

atoms.narrative: Hello, my name is Robert and I live in New York City. For breakfast I usually have pancakes, eggs and cereals. It is a big breakfast, but I need a lot of energy in the morning. For lunch I do not have much time, so I take cheese, chicken and vegetable sandwiches to the office. For dinner I like a salad with rice, carrots and peas, or some pasta. And for dessert, a little fruit and some chocolate.

atoms.prompt: Write a blog (about 100 words) and share your ideas about "Meals in Argentina".
atoms.modelAnswer: In Argentina we have four meals a day. Breakfast is small: usually coffee with milk and a few medialunas. Lunch is between twelve and two, and it is often meat with salad or a pasta dish. In the afternoon we have la merienda, with tea or mate and some biscuits. Dinner is late, after nine o’clock, and it is the main meal for many families. Our most traditional dishes are asado, empanadas and milanesa with mashed potatoes. Today many people eat less meat and more vegetables, but the asado on Sunday is still a family tradition.
modelVariants: Meals in Argentina are different from meals in Britain. We do not have a big breakfast: just coffee and a medialuna. Lunch is at one, dinner is after nine, and between them we have la merienda with mate. The typical dishes are asado, empanadas and milanesas. Nowadays some people eat more vegetables and less meat, but on Sundays the family still gets together for an asado.
scaffold: 1. Cuántas comidas hay por día en Argentina.
2. El desayuno: qué es y por qué es chico.
4. La merienda, que no existe en Gran Bretaña.
5. La cena: el horario tardío como rasgo argentino.
6. Los platos tradicionales y qué cambió hoy.

steps.hint: La merienda no tiene equivalente británico: vale nombrarla en español.

steps.segment: Dinner is late, after nine o’clock, and it is the main meal for many families.
steps.hint: El horario tardío es LO que sorprende a un extranjero.

steps.segment: Our most traditional dishes are asado, empanadas and milanesa with mashed potatoes.
Today many people eat less meat and more vegetables, but the asado on Sunday is still a family tradition.
steps.hint: El cierre: el contraste tradicional/actual, como en el texto de Gran Bretaña.

atoms.prompt: A foreign visitor asks you what a typical Argentinian dish is. Explain one.
atoms.modelAnswer: Let me tell you about the empanada. It is a small pie that you can hold in your hand. The pastry is made with flour, and inside there is a filling: usually minced meat with onion, egg and olives, but there are many kinds. Some people prefer chicken, cheese and onion, or corn. You can bake them in the oven or fry them in oil. We eat them with our hands, and a few empanadas are enough for a light dinner. Every province has its own recipe, and people argue a lot about which one is the best.
scaffold: 1. Anunciá qué plato vas a explicar.
2. Qué es, en una frase simple.
3. De qué está hecho: masa y relleno.
5. Cómo se cocina y cómo se come.

rubric.text: Usás incontables correctamente (flour, cheese, meat, oil)
Usás cuantificadores (some, a few, many, a lot of)
Cerrás con algo cultural, no solo la receta
